newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy ends strongly up on cool weather worries.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy ends strongly up on cool weather worries.

text.p: Concern about forecasts for cool weather soon in the U.S. Midwest boosted CBOT soybean futures to a strongly higher close, traders said.

"The belief is, even with a bearish report we're going to be better on beans anyway because we're going to frost them to death," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International. "You can't argue with them because that could happen."
Temperatures were expected to drop to below normal across much of the U.S. Midwest this week as a slow-moving cold front pushes across the region, meteorologists said.
U.S. soy lags normal maturity and conditions declined slightly last week.
USDA said the crop as of Sunday rated 55 percent good to excellent, down from 57 percent in that category the previous week.
New crop November reached a two-month high of $8.88 per bushel and ended near that level at $8.07, up 13-1/4 cents.
Buy stops were touched in the November early when that month pushed above $8.03, last week's high and an area of chart resistance, traders said.
Soybeans closed four to 13-1/4 cents per bushel higher, with September up 10 at $8.30.

The market was poised for a slow day before the release at 0730 Wednesday of USDA's September crop production report. An average of analysts' estimates pegged the 1996 U.S. soybean crop at 2.240 billion bushels, below USDA's forecast in August for 2.3 billion.
But fund buying coupled with reminders late Monday of the vulnerability of the soybean crop to cold weather boosted the market and demand was broad based.

Smith Barney bought three million bushels of November, Rosenthal Collins bought two million November with numerous other firms plus locals purchasing from one half million to one million bushels in the November, they said.
Volume was estimated at 45,000, up from 33,139 Monday, according to the CBOT.

In the soybean options pit, Smith Barney bought 1,000 November $7.50 puts and sold 1,000 November $7.75 puts at 7-1/2 cents, traders said. Smith Barney also bought 1,000 November $7.50 puts and sold 1,000 November $8.00 puts at 20 cents, they said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 30,000, up from 18,476 Monday.
